stem: A client with prior liver disease is receiving systemic fluconazole and develops rising aminotransferases. What should the nurse recognize?

options.A: Recognize possible fluconazole-associated hepatic injury and ensure worsening liver injury is monitored when liver tests become abnormal.
options.B: Assume fluconazole has no clinically important hepatic effects even when the client’s liver tests are rising.
options.C: Ignore abnormal liver tests unless blood glucose is also elevated during the antifungal treatment course.
options.D: Assume fluconazole liver injury occurs only after a predictable cumulative dose and therefore cannot occur earlier in therapy.

rationale: DailyMed fluconazole labeling warns that fluconazole should be used cautiously in patients with liver dysfunction and has been associated with rare serious hepatic toxicity. The label specifically states that patients who develop abnormal liver function tests during therapy should be monitored for more severe hepatic injury; if clinical signs and symptoms consistent with fluconazole-attributable liver disease develop, the drug should be discontinued. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize rising liver tests during fluconazole therapy as a potential hepatic-safety signal requiring monitoring for more severe injury and appropriate escalation if clinical liver disease develops.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
source_version_date: Current DailyMed fluconazole labeling; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Warnings > Hepatic Injury: caution in liver dysfunction; rare serious hepatic toxicity; no obvious relationship to dose or duration; abnormal liver-function tests require monitoring for more severe hepatic injury; discontinue if attributable clinical liver-disease signs/symptoms develop.
source_claim_supported: Fluconazole can cause serious hepatic toxicity; patients who develop abnormal liver tests during therapy should be monitored for progression to more severe hepatic injury.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: identify adverse effects and contraindications, monitor medication response, and provide safe medication care.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — fluconazole hepatic toxicity and monitoring

source_original.stem: A client with prior liver disease is receiving systemic fluconazole and develops rising aminotransferases. What should the nurse recognize?

options.A: Recognize possible hepatic toxicity and monitor worsening liver injury when liver tests become abnormal
options.B: Assume fluconazole has no important hepatic effects even when the client's liver tests are rising
options.C: Ignore abnormal liver tests unless blood glucose is also elevated during the antifungal treatment course
options.D: Assume liver injury occurs only after a predictable cumulative dose and cannot occur earlier in therapy

source_original.rationale: Fluconazole labeling warns of rare serious hepatic toxicity and advises caution in patients with liver dysfunction. Patients who develop abnormal liver function tests during therapy should be monitored for more severe hepatic injury, and the drug should be discontinued if clinical signs or symptoms of liver disease attributable to fluconazole develop.
source_original.source_detail: Warnings, Hepatic Injury: caution with liver dysfunction; monitor patients with abnormal liver function tests for more severe hepatic injury.

correction_summary: Retained key A and the hepatic-toxicity construct, tightened the nursing interpretation to monitoring/escalation rather than independently ordering discontinuation, verified the exact hepatic-injury warning against the source label and current fluconazole labeling, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: DailyMed official fluconazole labeling; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: Source label remains live; current 2026 DailyMed fluconazole labeling carries the same hepatic-injury warning and was live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately links rising aminotransferases to a known fluconazole hepatic-safety risk and preserves the label's distinction between abnormal tests requiring monitoring and clinical liver disease prompting discontinuation.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because serious hepatic toxicity is a labeled risk.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because hepatic monitoring is not contingent on glucose elevation.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because labeling states no obvious relationship to total daily dose or duration of therapy.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A correctly interprets the abnormal liver tests in the context of fluconazole therapy.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives interpret the same laboratory change; A is keyed by label evidence rather than option form.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — adverse-effect recognition and monitoring.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the source DailyMed hepatic-injury warning and a current 2026 fluconazole label, then all choices, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
